subject.title: feat: bound transcript reads across replacements

question: Should OpenClaw establish generation-aware raw and visible transcript cursors as permanent public Plugin SDK APIs, with persistent generation state, or keep bounded transcript reading internal until concrete owner plugins require a shared contract?
rationale: The implementation can be mechanically tested, but only maintainers can choose whether these exported cursor semantics and persisted upgrade behavior are a supported long-term platform contract.

options.title: Keep the scope internal
options.body: Retain or rework the active-memory bounded read behind an owner-specific/internal seam and defer public cursors plus durable generation state until a concrete shared caller requires them.

options.title: Sponsor the public contract
options.body: Explicitly accept the raw and visible cursor APIs, document their reset and upgrade guarantees, and revise persistence to follow the additive-table migration policy before merge.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Close or pause this foundation and its dependent proposals until maintainers define a transcript pagination and plugin API roadmap.

recommendation.title: Keep the scope internal
recommendation.body: Retain or rework the active-memory bounded read behind an owner-specific/internal seam and defer public cursors plus durable generation state until a concrete shared caller requires them.

likelyOwner.reason: This is an architecture and public-platform decision spanning agent persistence, plugin compatibility, and the linked follow-up stack.
